title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 40
paragraphs: After this deed they spent two more days, neither side willing to begin a battle; for the barbarians advanced as far as the Asopos to test the Greeks, but neither side would cross the river. However, Mardonius's cavalry made attacks continually and did damage to the Greeks; for the Thebans, strongly on the Medes' side, pressed the war with vigor, and always led the way up to the moment of fighting; and after this, the Persians and Medes took up the work and were the ones who displayed valor in their turn.
